Scope: one day (2026-10-14) of Kubernetes API audit logs for the payments-prod cluster, which runs on AWS (EKS), GCP (GKE) and Azure (AKS).

Data: tables raw_eks, raw_gke and raw_aks hold each cloud's audit log export exactly as that cloud delivers it. Enrichment tables (identities, identity_links, service_accounts, clusters, privileged_allowlist, approved_registries, ip_reputation) describe people, service accounts, assets and IP reputation.

Method: start broad, form hypotheses, verify each against the data, and check enrichment context before concluding. Cite every malicious event you rely on by its audit event ID. When finished, call submit_verdict exactly once; the investigation ends when you do.

input.summary: Jordan Doe (jdoe@example.com, Payments Engineering) is on PTO from 2026-10-12 to 2026-10-19 and normally works from a darwin client. His credentials were used from 198.51.100.23, a bulletproof VPS host (NIGHTOWL-HOSTING, NL) that threat feeds tag for K8s API brute-forcing and for running an open Docker registry on port 5000. The same 12-step attack ran on all three payments-prod clusters, in order: EKS 14:02–14:25, GKE 14:38–15:01, AKS 15:11–15:34. Each time the actor checked its permissions, tried kube-system secrets and a Job (both blocked with 403), read payments/payments-db-credentials, started a privileged alpine pod 'debug-tools-7f9c' and used nsenter to break out to the node. From the node it took the argocd-application-controller service-account token, which has cluster-admin. With that token, from the outside IP, it created ClusterRoleBinding 'jdoe-break-glass' giving jdoe's principal cluster-admin. It then set up persistence with images pulled from its own registry (198.51.100.23:5000): a DaemonSet 'kube-metrics-agent' and a CronJob 'node-cert-rotate', both in kube-system, plus a NodePort service 'metrics-agent-np' on port 30080. Finally it listed secrets across the whole cluster, which is what fired the alert. All three clouds are fully compromised. Every secret, including the payments DB credentials, should be treated as stolen; jdoe's access and the ArgoCD token need to be revoked and rotated; and the binding, DaemonSet, CronJob, service and debug pod must be removed on every cluster.

verdict.summary: Jordan Doe (jdoe@example.com, Payments Engineering) is on PTO from 2026-10-12 to 2026-10-19 and normally works from a darwin client. His credentials were used from 198.51.100.23, a bulletproof VPS host (NIGHTOWL-HOSTING, NL) that threat feeds tag for K8s API brute-forcing and for running an open Docker registry on port 5000. The same 12-step attack ran on all three payments-prod clusters, in order: EKS 14:02–14:25, GKE 14:38–15:01, AKS 15:11–15:34. Each time the actor checked its permissions, tried kube-system secrets and a Job (both blocked with 403), read payments/payments-db-credentials, started a privileged alpine pod 'debug-tools-7f9c' and used nsenter to break out to the node. From the node it took the argocd-application-controller service-account token, which has cluster-admin. With that token, from the outside IP, it created ClusterRoleBinding 'jdoe-break-glass' giving jdoe's principal cluster-admin. It then set up persistence with images pulled from its own registry (198.51.100.23:5000): a DaemonSet 'kube-metrics-agent' and a CronJob 'node-cert-rotate', both in kube-system, plus a NodePort service 'metrics-agent-np' on port 30080. Finally it listed secrets across the whole cluster, which is what fired the alert. All three clouds are fully compromised. Every secret, including the payments DB credentials, should be treated as stolen; jdoe's access and the ArgoCD token need to be revoked and rotated; and the binding, DaemonSet, CronJob, service and debug pod must be removed on every cluster.
